gen-gf-autour-one-gf-lexend-zetta: Expressive and loud, Autour One pushes round letters forward with a clear channel leading into each curve. Lexend Zetta follows in widely tracked sans, its ribbon-like strokes holding one width from end to end.
gen-megrim-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code sits in the body, modern and wire-thin. Megrim above it is angular and futuristic, every stroke ending at one measured thickness, with a tall x-height line.
gen-megrim-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads as a compact, professional sans-serif where capitals melt into lowercase and letters stand like pins in a wide board. Megrim's angular, measured strokes above it stay sharp.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-montserrat-alternates: Gugi's lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. And Montserrat Alternates carries on below with round letters whose rims match their stems, crowding gently toward the capital line.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-lexend-exa: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, with c tips that never creep toward touching. And Lexend Exa, a professional sans-serif, answers with a big x-height and stubby ascenders that keep its curves distinct.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-lexend-mega: Goldman arrives widely set, bold and generous with clearance. Lexend Mega, a plain sans, looks drawn with one nib, so no thick-to-thin shift slows the eye against Goldman's roomy forms.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads approachable and professional, its c shapes wide like an open mouth and its curves never thinning. Grandstander, by contrast, brings the bold, expressive lines up top, held open rather than curled shut, with short ascenders over a tall x-height.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-lexend-t: Love Ya Like A Sister keeps its ascenders barely clearing the x-height, with terminal tips pointing outward and no accents of weight. Lexend Tera, a plain sans, draws like a plotter pen, letters spaced like stepping stones.
gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-lexend-zetta: Stately, a bit strange, and widely spaced. Lexend Zetta, a sans-serif with constant-width strokes like a sign-painter's brush, sits against Metamorphous, whose fat and slim strokes shift gently like tapered glass rods.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-montserrat-alternates: Scattered, loud letters fill the line like capitals. And Montserrat Alternates, a sans-serif with a bent-paperclip c and no thick-thin shifts, feels like a tidy, contemporary neighbor to Paprika's hollow-reed counters.
